text:
anya: heads up — after the kernel-routing tweak we pushed last night I'm seeing a 2–3x P50 regression on a subset of long-seq workloads. attached nsys shows a tight hotspot on a fallback kernel that didn't used to be on the hot path.

sam: can you paste the nsys cmd and the short timeline screenshot?

anya: ran:
```
nsys profile --output nvtx_trace --sample=none --force-overwrite 
  --trace=nvtx,cuda,kernel --output-dir=/tmp/traces/2765 /opt/inference/bin/runner --model gpt-like --seq 2048 --batch 8
```
link: perfetto://local/2765432100/timeline (perm:eng-runtime)

chris: quick glance — looks like kernel selector started preferring matmul_fused_v2 for certain shapes, but the chosen launch config forces a global memcopy on the KV path. that memcopy serializes KV refill and stalls the main compute.

val: hmm that sounds like the affinity change we made to prefer low-latency variants on smaller micro-batches. could be a shape/stride mismatch. did you bisect to a range?

anya: i did a quick bisect: regression introduced between commits abc1f2 -> abc1f7 (selector refactor + affinity heuristic). reduced test case to reproduce in 60s. bisect notes: selector patch swapped kernel preference order but forgot to check kv_stride for fallback.

perf-bot: flamegraph summary attached: top stacks: matmul_fused_v2::launch -> cudaMemcpyAsync (KV refill) [50%], softmax_attn_fast [18%], allocator_wait [12%]

sam: can you run the same workload with selector override to force the old kernel? i.e. env KERNEL_POLICY=legacy_selector ./runner ...

anya: did that. forcing legacy kernel restores baseline latency and removes the memcpy hotspot. numbers: baseline P50 45ms -> regressed 110ms -> forced-legacy 48ms.

chris: looks like a straightforward fix: add kv_stride check into the new preference comparator and add a unit test that runs the small-batch long-seq path. also add an nsys assertion in CI to catch memcpy appearing in hot path for critical workloads.

val: agree. i'll open a PR with comparator guard + test. val: tagging @sam for review.

anya: created draft PR 2782 with patch + perf trace in description. marking this thread for follow-up after CI runs. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: nice find. after PR lands we should run a full perfetto contrast (before/after) and add a note to the rollout playbook about kernel-affinity changes.

anya: noted. i'll attach before/after perfetto links to the PR and ping infra for a 2-hour canary run on dedicated capacity.

perf-bot: CI trace check failed on master for this workload (memcpy-hotspot detected). triggering rollback candidate flagged.

chris: perfect — that's the safety net we wanted. we'll keep this open until canary looks clean.

anya: closing loop: temporary rollback scheduled for next deploy window if canary >2% error on latency. will update thread with post-canary numbers.
